title: Apps & installing
blurb: Installing and removing apps, Store problems, apps that won't start.

remedies.title: An app won't install
remedies.why: Not enough space, no admin rights, an older version in the way, or the installer is for another system (32/64-bit, Intel/Apple silicon).

steps.text: Check free disk space.
Get the installer again from the maker's site, choosing the right version (Windows x64/ARM, Mac Apple silicon/Intel).
Uninstall an older version first.
Restart, then run the installer again (a pending update can block installs).
If it asks for an admin password you don't have, ask IT or the computer's owner.

remedies.escalate: Give IT the installer's name and the exact error.

remedies.title: Uninstall an app
remedies.why: Removing apps you don't use frees space and stops them running in the background.

steps.text: Settings › Apps › Installed apps › ⋯ › Uninstall.
Drag the app from Applications to the Bin; for apps with their own uninstaller (in the app's folder), use that.
If an app won't uninstall, its maker often has a removal tool on their support site.

remedies.title: Microsoft Store won't open, download or update
remedies.why: The Store's cache is damaged, the clock is wrong, or Windows Update is stuck.

steps.text: Reset the Store's cache.
Correct the date and time.
Sign out of the Store and back in (your picture at the top).
Settings › Apps › Installed apps › Microsoft Store › Advanced options › Repair, then Reset.

remedies.title: App Store won't download or update apps
remedies.why: A stuck download, sign-in problem, or not enough space.

steps.text: Check free space.
In the App Store, Store › Sign Out, then sign in again.
Pause and resume the download from Launchpad, or restart the Mac.

remedies.title: An app won't open or closes straight away
symptoms: nothing happens when i open app
remedies.why: Damaged settings, a missing component, a pending update, or it's already running in the background.

steps.text: Check it isn't already running (taskbar/menu bar icons) and close that copy.
Restart the computer.
Settings › Apps › the app › Advanced options › Repair, then Reset (Store apps); or Modify › Repair for desktop apps.
Update or reinstall the app.
Check Reliability Monitor for the error.
Look in Console › Crash Reports for the app's report.

remedies.title: "MSVCP140.dll / VCRUNTIME140.dll is missing" or .NET errors
remedies.why: The app needs a Microsoft runtime (Visual C++ Redistributable or .NET) that isn't installed or is damaged.

steps.text: Install the latest Visual C++ Redistributable (x64 and x86) from Microsoft's site (search "Visual C++ Redistributable latest").
For .NET messages, install the version named in the message from dotnet.microsoft.com, or turn on .NET Framework 3.5 in Windows features.
Never download single DLL files from "DLL download" sites.

remedies.title: Files open in the wrong app
remedies.why: Each file type has a default app, which installs can change.

steps.text: Settings › Apps › Default apps › search the file type (.pdf, .jpg) and pick the app.
Right-click a file › Get Info › Open with › choose › Change All.

remedies.title: Stop apps starting with the computer
remedies.why: Many apps add themselves to startup, slowing the start and using memory.

steps.text: Settings › Apps › Startup: turn off what you don't need right away.
System Settings › General › Login Items & Extensions: remove apps and turn off background items.
Keep security software, cloud sync and anything IT installed.
